Generate isomorphs from item models

Source: R/ai-aig.R
generate_isomorphs.Rd

Fills the templates of one or more item models (item_model()) with combinations of their values that meet the constraints, and returns the generated items with their options in random order. Each item keeps the values it was generated from, which are its features for calibration and for predict_difficulty().

Usage

generate_isomorphs(model, n = 10, seed = 1, shuffle = TRUE, drop_flawed = TRUE)

Arguments

model

an item model, or a list of item models.

n

number of isomorphs per model; NULL generates every combination of values.

seed

random seed for the choice of values and the order of the options, or NULL.

shuffle

logical; put the options in random order. Otherwise the key is option A.

drop_flawed

logical; drop items whose options are not all different.

Value

A tibble with one row per item: id, model, stem, the options A, B, ..., key (the letter of the correct option), one column per variable, and flag. It can be passed to add_items(), item_features() and review_packet().

Details

Combinations that give two identical options, or that cannot be computed, would make flawed items: By default they are left out of the pool that isomorphs are drawn from, with a message, so that the constraints can be fixed. With drop_flawed = FALSE, combinations with identical options stay in the pool and their items are marked in the flag column.

See also

item_model(), calibrate_families().

Examples

speed <- item_model(
  stem = "A car travels {s * t} km in {t} hours. What is its average speed?",
  key = "{s} km/h",
  distractors = c(multiplied = "{s * t * t} km/h", subtracted = "{s * t - t} km/h",
                  distance = "{s * t} km/h"),
  values = list(s = seq(40, 90, 10), t = 2:5), name = "SPD")
generate_isomorphs(speed, n = 4)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 11
#>   id     model stem              A     B     C     D     key       s     t flag 
#>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>             <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <dbl> <int> <chr>
#> 1 SPD-01 SPD   A car travels 80… 40 k… 78 k… 80 k… 160 … A        40     2 ""   
#> 2 SPD-02 SPD   A car travels 10… 200 … 98 k… 50 k… 100 … C        50     2 ""   
#> 3 SPD-03 SPD   A car travels 14… 70 k… 140 … 280 … 138 … A        70     2 ""   
#> 4 SPD-04 SPD   A car travels 12… 360 … 120 … 40 k… 117 … C        40     3 ""
